validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via two genuinely independent origins. (1) Uztransgaz's own Dec 30, 2022 announcement of construction start, carried near-identically by gazeta.uz, tashkenttimes.uz and uz.sputniknews.ru (all three cite the same '47 km of pipe delivered, 6 km installed, Q3 2023 target' figures and Sputnik explicitly attributes the numbers to Uztransgaz/Minenergy — this is one wire story republished three times, not three independent confirmations, per standing rule 4). (2) The EPC contractor's own channel, Enter Engineering Pte. Ltd.'s Telegram (t.me/enterengineeringpteltd/4500, undated but post-Dec-2022), independently describing active work 'на участке Янгиер — Ахангаран' with 270 workers and 100 pieces of equipment, naming Uztransgaz as the modernization program's customer via LLC Transgazengineering. Two different organizational origins (state gas company vs. private EPC contractor) = existence is solid. CLASSIFICATION: correct. Gazeta.uz calls it a 'магистральный газопровод' (main/trunk gas pipeline) carrying gas — matches PipelineType=transmission, Fuel=Gas. DUPLICATE: checked against sibling P6964 (same PipelineName, Segment I, operating, same Yangiyer->Ahangaran endpoints, no length/diameter recorded). NOT a duplicate — the Sept 30, 2023 gazeta.uz follow-up (https://www.gazeta.uz/ru/2023/09/30/uztransgaz/) explicitly calls P6963 a 'новая нитка' (new [parallel] line/string), which is standard Uzbek/Soviet pipeline terminology for one of several parallel strings in a corridor (the same term used for the Gazli-Kagan 4-string family in this country's roster) — i.e. it is described as a second, additional line alongside an existing one, exactly matching GEM's own Segment I/II split. RouteNotes on the sheet already independently notes 'will run parallel to segment I.' SPEC: length=95 km and diameter=1220 mm are stated identically in the Dec 2022 launch coverage and repeated in the Sept 2023 follow-up — no numeric conflict found anywhere. However both dated mentions trace to Uztransgaz as the sole underlying origin (state monopoly, no independent line-wise register exists per country guidance), so tier is medium, not high — an honest read, not a failure to search (Russian-language search was exhausted; utg.uz's own site has been restructured and every old deep-link to its press archive, including the specific Yangiyer-Akhangaran launch article, now 404s or soft-404s to a generic news list, so Uztransgaz's own primary announcement could not be re-verified directly — only via the gazeta.uz/tashkenttimes syndication). STATUS: see status_reviews below (confirm — still under construction, no completion evidence found).

validity.recommendation: Verify/correct StartState/Province: likely Sirdaryo Region, not Fergana. Do not apply blind — the exact compressor-station location, not just the city center, should be pinned down first.
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded StartState/Province for the 'Yangiyer' endpoint is 'Fergana.' The only source for that is gem.wiki's own infobox text ('Yangiyer Compressor Station, Fergana region') — no independent source found names a Fergana-region facility called Yangiyer. Independently: the well-documented city of Yangiyer (English Wikipedia, verified) is unambiguously in Sirdaryo Region (coords 40.267N, 68.817E), not Fergana. Straight-line distance from Yangiyer city to Akhangaran (Tashkent Region, confirmed via Wikipedia) is ~108 km — MORE than the pipeline's own recorded length of 95 km, which is geometrically implausible if downtown Yangiyer is the true start anchor (a pipeline route cannot be shorter than the straight-line distance between its endpoints). Network logic also favors Sirdaryo: Yangiyer sits on/near the historic Bukhara-Tashkent-Bishkek-Almaty trunk corridor (P6933-P6935, excluded from this batch) that runs through Sirdaryo Region, with this pipeline reading as a lateral tie-in branching southeast into Tashkent Region (Akhangaran) and onward via the Kamchik pass into the Fergana Valley (the P4071/P4072 Ahangaran-Pungan pipeline) — i.e. 'improves gas supply to the Fergana Valley' (the pipeline's stated PURPOSE/destination, per gazeta.uz) is likely being conflated with the start point's own province. RouteAccuracy is already 'no route' and RouteNotes already says exact start/end points are unknown, so this is flagged as an open attribution question rather than an auto-correction — no source directly states the compressor station's province, so I'm not fabricating a replacement value, just flagging the current one as unsupported and likely wrong.

fills.researcher_notes: Operator [ref] was blank (MISSING_REF) though Operator=Uztransgaz was already recorded and matches the Owner tab. Two independent sources confirm Uztransgaz as the entity building/operating this line: gazeta.uz's Dec 30, 2022 announcement of Uztransgaz launching construction, and Enter Engineering's own Telegram post naming Uztransgaz (via customer LLC Transgazengineering) as the modernization program's principal on this exact section.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched Russian- and English-language sources for any evidence the pipeline has been completed/commissioned since its Dec 2022 construction start (original target was Q3 2023). Found none. The most recent VERIFIABLE, dated evidence of continued construction is the Sept 30, 2023 gazeta.uz mention of 'строительство новой нитки протяжённостью 95 км по направлению Янгиер-Ахангаран' (construction of a new 95 km line, still framed as ongoing, ~9 months past the original Q3-2023 target — i.e. already delayed at that point). Additional undated corroboration: Enter Engineering's Telegram post (t.me/enterengineeringpteltd/4500) describes the Yangiyer-Ahangaran section work as having 'entered a decisive/final phase' ('в решающую фазу вступил') with 270 workers and 100 units of equipment — clearly later than Sept 2023 given the escalated framing, but I could not extract an exact date from Telegram's rendered timestamps (time-of-day only, no calendar date in the fetched view), so I am not using it as the evidence_date anchor. The sheet's own current_ref (Instagram, Aug 23 2025, retrieved Sept 5 2025 by researcher AV) is consistent with 'still construction, not yet complete' but its content could not be independently re-verified — Instagram is JS-rendered and url_verifier could not confirm the 'construction' token on the page (existing_ref_checks already flags this: '200 but data value not found'). No source anywhere — Uzbek press, contractor channel, or gem.wiki's own citation list — claims commissioning/completion. Given continued (if undated) contractor activity and zero completion evidence, 'construction' is confirmed as still correct rather than stale; this is a live, actively-worked project, not a dormant one, so the 2y/4y staleness rules do not apply.

summary: P6963 (Yangiyer-Ahangaran Gas Pipeline, Segment II): existence/classification/spec/non-duplicate all confirmed (caveat) — genuinely a second, parallel 'new line' alongside operating Segment I P6964, not a double count; ONE new concern raised (attribution: StartState/Province likely Sirdaryo, not Fergana, per Yangiyer city's real location + a length-vs-distance inconsistency); Operator [ref] filled (2 independent sources, high tier); status review = confirm (still construction, no completion evidence found).
